subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats automatically provision per-sender subagents with isolated skills/config/memory, or should sender-scoped group sessions remain the supported isolation model while subagent, skill, and memory policy are tracked separately?
rationale: Current source has partial session and thread-binding infrastructure, but the requested default architecture changes channel routing, agent lifecycle, memory isolation, skills, config writes, and security boundaries.

options.title: Keep As Feishu Design Umbrella
options.body: Use this issue as the product/security decision point for automatic Feishu group sender subagents, then split any approved design into narrow implementation issues.

options.title: Narrow To Session Scopes
options.body: Treat group_sender and group_topic_sender as the supported current model and close or rewrite the automatic per-user subagent parts as out of scope.

options.title: Defer To Related APIs
options.body: Resolve Feishu account identity, channel threading policy, and user skill preferences in their related issues before revisiting automatic group subagents.

recommendation.title: Keep As Feishu Design Umbrella
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the product/security decision point for automatic Feishu group sender subagents, then split any approved design into narrow implementation issues.

likelyOwner.reason: They most directly own the current Feishu session, dynamic-agent, and subagent-hook code paths involved in this decision.
